calls.summary: Maria Delgado called to request a second opinion for newly diagnosed breast cancer. Agent Oscar confirmed no referral was needed, collected her records details, and scheduled a new patient consultation at the Tampa campus. Maria left reassured and confirmed her appointment date.

Robert Chen asked whether Moffitt offers immunotherapy and CAR T-cell therapy for his lung cancer. Agent Lila explained the immunotherapy options and financial counseling resources, then booked a new patient consultation with the thoracic oncology team. Robert scheduled his visit before ending the call.

Patricia Nguyen called about the status of her hereditary genetic testing panel results. Agent Rosey located the order, confirmed the lab was still processing the panel, and offered to have the genetic counselor follow up. Patricia was satisfied with the timeline and did not need a new appointment.

James Whitaker called as a prospective new patient seeking a second opinion after a colorectal cancer diagnosis. Agent Mary walked him through the intake process, collected his insurance and demographic details, and scheduled his first appointment with a surgical oncologist. James enrolled in the MyMoffitt portal before hanging up.

Karen Foster inquired about low-dose CT lung cancer screening because she is a former smoker. Agent Lee confirmed she met the criteria and booked her screening appointment at the outpatient center. Karen appreciated the quick scheduling and cost estimate information.

Daniel Ortiz called disputing a billing statement for his recent chemotherapy cycle. Agent Sue reviewed the charges, explained the insurance adjustment, and connected him to a financial counselor for a payment plan. Daniel remained frustrated about the amount but accepted the follow-up.

Angela Rivera asked whether she qualified for a Phase 1 clinical trial for her glioblastoma. Agent Mike reviewed the eligibility questions and scheduled a candidacy consultation with the clinical research unit. Angela was hopeful and confirmed the appointment.

Thomas Reilly called to reschedule his PET imaging appointment due to a conflict. Agent Jennifer found an earlier slot but the system was slow to confirm, causing a short delay. Thomas got his new imaging time but noted the wait on hold.

Linda Park requested genetic testing because of a strong family history of ovarian cancer. Agent Rose explained the counselor consult requirement and booked her genetic counseling appointment. Linda was a bit confused about the two-step process but scheduled the visit.

Gregory Sanders called upset about a duplicate billing charge for radiation therapy. Agent Oscar could not immediately locate the second charge and had to escalate to the billing department. Gregory ended the call still waiting for a resolution.

Nancy Coleman asked general questions about mammography screening costs but was not ready to book. Agent Lila provided the cost estimate resource and screening criteria but Nancy declined to schedule. She said she would call back after checking with her insurance.

Frank Bishop complained about the long wait to hear back on his clinical trial candidacy review. Agent Lee apologized and could only confirm the research team would follow up soon. Frank remained dissatisfied and did not schedule anything.

Sandra Mitchell called seeking a second opinion for bladder cancer but was frustrated by transfers between departments. Agent Sue eventually collected her information and scheduled a consultation. Sandra booked the visit but expressed annoyance about the runaround.

Walter Simmons left a voicemail asking about immunotherapy options for prostate cancer after hours. The call rolled to voicemail and no agent was available to assist. No appointment was scheduled and a callback was requested.

Deborah Hayes called to cancel her upcoming surgical consultation and voiced anger about a scheduling mix-up. Agent Mike processed the cancellation but could not resolve her complaint about the earlier error. Deborah hung up dissatisfied and did not rebook.

prompts.question: Is the patient trying to solve a specific problem?
prompts.answer: Yes. The caller is a new patient seeking an initial consultation and diagnostic workup for breast cancer. She found Moffitt through a web search and wants to schedule an appointment with an oncologist as soon as possible.

prompts.question: What are the patient's expectations?
prompts.answer: The caller expects a prompt appointment, confirmation that she will be evaluated in the Tampa Bay area, and clarity on what to bring and what the first visit will involve. She is anxious and wants reassurance about the next steps.

prompts.question: How could the agent handle the call better?
prompts.answer: The agent should have asked for the patient's email address to send appointment confirmation and pre-visit paperwork, and should have documented the referral source (organic search) for marketing attribution. Adding a brief statement about what to expect during the first visit would have reduced patient anxiety.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello and thank you for calling Moffitt Cancer Center. My name is Marcus Bell. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Marcus. I need to schedule an appointment. I was recently diagnosed with breast cancer and a friend recommended I call you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm sorry to hear about your diagnosis. We're so glad you reached out to us. I'd be happy to help you schedule an appointment. May I have your full name please?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, it's Sarah Mitchell. M-I-T-C-H-E-L-L.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you Sarah. And are you currently covered by an insurance plan, or would you prefer to discuss self-pay options?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I have Blue Cross Blue Shield insurance through my employer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. That's very helpful information. Sarah, just to confirm, you're looking to schedule an initial consultation with one of our breast cancer oncologists here at Moffitt, correct?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. I want to get started as soon as possible. I'm really anxious to understand my treatment options.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I completely understand. We have availability this coming Monday and Wednesday. Are either of those days convenient for you?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Monday would work great for me. What time do you have?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent. We have a 10 a.m. slot on Monday, October 21st. Does that work with your schedule?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, 10 a.m. is perfect.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful Sarah. I need to confirm your phone number to reach you if we need to reschedule. Can you provide that?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. I have you down for Monday, October 21st at 10 a.m. at our main clinic in Tampa. Please bring your insurance card and a list of any current medications. Do you have any other questions for me?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: No, I think that covers everything. I'm looking forward to meeting with the team.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's wonderful Sarah. Thank you for choosing Moffitt Cancer Center. Your appointment is confirmed for Monday at 10 a.m. We'll see you then. Have a great day.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Thank you, Marcus. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Goodbye Sarah.

callDetail.aiSummary: Sarah Mitchell, a newly diagnosed breast cancer patient with Blue Cross Blue Shield insurance, called Moffitt Cancer Center to schedule an initial consultation with an oncology specialist. Marcus Bell completed the intake by capturing her name, insurance information, and confirming a new patient appointment for Monday, October 21st at 10 a.m. at the Tampa location. While the agent successfully booked the appointment and provided basic pre-visit instructions, he did not capture her email address or referral source, and did not discuss what the patient should expect during the consultation to help manage her anxiety.

comment.author: Kyle Paklaian
comment.text: @Marcus Great structured intake call with Sarah. You nailed the greeting, captured all her core details, and communicated empathy when she mentioned her anxiety. Two coaching notes for next time: (1) Always ask for the patient's email address so we can send appointment confirmation and any pre-visit forms electronically. (2) Before closing, take 15 seconds to briefly describe what to expect at her first visit, like 'You'll meet with our breast cancer specialist, we'll review your pathology reports, and you'll discuss initial treatment options.' This reduces patient stress and increases show-up rates. You've got great instincts with this patient. Keep it up.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Moffitt Cancer Center, Florida's number one chance for beating cancer. This is Denise. How can I help you today?
highlights: Thank you for calling Moffitt Cancer Center
How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Denise. My name is Robert Alvarez. I was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer and I'm trying to figure out how to become a patient there and get a second opinion.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm so sorry to hear about your diagnosis, Robert, and I'm glad you reached out. The good news is you do not need a referral to get a second opinion with us. Can I start by getting your full name and a callback number?
highlights: you do not need a referral

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Sure, it's Robert Alvarez, and my cell is 813-555-0172. I've been reading about immunotherapy and something called CAR T, and I wanted to know if those are options for me.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great, thank you. For lung cancer our thoracic oncology team frequently uses immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors, and they'll also run precision medicine tumor profiling to see if a targeted therapy fits your specific mutations.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Okay, that's helpful. But honestly I have to ask, what does that run? I want to keep this manageable, my insurance is decent but I've heard these treatments get really expensive.
highlights: I want to keep this manageable

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's a fair question. Most costs are billed through your insurance and Medicare, and we have a team that will obtain a cost estimate and walk you through your coverage before anything begins. You'll never be surprised by a bill you didn't plan for.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That helps. I'll be honest, I'm also looking at a center up in Atlanta that a friend recommended, so I'm getting a couple of opinions before I commit.
highlights: I'm getting a couple of opinions before I commit

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's completely understandable, and getting more than one opinion is smart. What sets Moffitt apart is that we're a National Cancer Institute designated Comprehensive Cancer Center, and we have clinical trials and Phase 1 options right here in Tampa if standard treatment isn't the best path.
highlights: National Cancer Institute designated Comprehensive Cancer Center

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Clinical trials, that's actually something I wanted to ask about too. Would I even be a candidate for one of those?
highlights: Would I even be a candidate

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Possibly, and our team can review that during your visit through our Am I A Candidate assessment. The best next step is to get you scheduled with a thoracic oncologist. I have an opening this Thursday at 10 AM at our Magnolia campus. Does that work?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Thursday could work, but I'd want to run it by my wife first since she's coming with me. Can I lock that in for now?
highlights: run it by my wife first

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Absolutely, I'll reserve Thursday at 10 AM for you and send the details to MyMoffitt so you can confirm once you check with her. Please bring any imaging and pathology records from your current provider.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Perfect, thank you so much Denise. This makes me feel a lot better.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome, Robert. Your appointment is set for Thursday at 10 AM and we'll see you and your wife then. Take care and reach out anytime.
highlights: Your appointment is set for Thursday at 10 AM
Take care and reach out anytime.

transcript.text: Hi there. Thanks for reaching out to Moffitt Cancer Center. This is Sarah from our new patient team. Are you calling about scheduling a consultation or getting a second opinion on your care?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Yes, hi. I was diagnosed with stage 2 breast cancer last month and my doctor suggested I get a second opinion. My friend recommended Moffitt.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm so glad you reached out. Moffitt is Florida's top cancer center and we specialize in breast cancer treatment. To help you best, have you already had genetic testing done for hereditary cancer risk factors like BRCA mutations?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: No, I haven't had that yet. My doctor said it might be something to consider.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's a great point to explore. Many patients find genetic counseling and testing really helpful for personalized treatment planning. Besides genetic testing, are you interested in exploring multiple treatment options including surgery, radiation, chemotherapy, or targeted therapy with our oncology team?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Definitely. I want to know all my options before deciding on a treatment plan.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. Our comprehensive breast cancer program includes surgical oncology, medical oncology, radiation therapy, and precision medicine to match your tumor profile to the best treatment. What's most convenient for you, a consultation here at our main Tampa facility or one of our outpatient centers in the greater Tampa Bay area?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Tampa works for me since I live there.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent. Our second opinion consultations are typically scheduled within 1 to 2 weeks. Would Tuesday, March 18th at 10:00 AM work for your initial consultation with one of our breast cancer specialists?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: That works perfectly.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful. I've scheduled your appointment for Tuesday, March 18th at 10:00 AM at our Tampa facility with Dr. Lisa Chen, one of our leading breast surgical oncologists. Please bring your recent imaging and pathology reports. You'll receive a confirmation call at this number in the next 24 hours. Our main line is 1-888-663-3488 if you have any questions. Thanks for choosing Moffitt Cancer Center.

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Great, thank you so much. I really appreciate the help.

Qualify one question at a time: Ask, one at a time, about the cancer type or reason for the visit, whether they are seeking a new patient evaluation or a second opinion, their insurance carrier, how soon they want to be seen, and finally their ZIP code so we can confirm the closest Tampa Bay location.

Confirm then book: Confirm we serve their area and can see them at a Tampa Bay campus, explain that our Patient Access and financial counseling teams provide insurance verification and cost estimates rather than a fixed price, recommend a new patient consultation with a subspecialty oncologist, propose a specific day and time, and confirm they will receive a reminder text with the 1-888-663-3488 line to call before the appointment.

qaPairs.question: Do I need a referral to become a patient at Moffitt?
qaPairs.answer: No physician referral is required to become a new patient at Moffitt Cancer Center. I can help you start a new patient consultation whenever you are ready.

qaPairs.question: How do I get a second opinion at Moffitt?
qaPairs.answer: Many patients come to us specifically for a second opinion from a subspecialty oncologist. Let's book a new patient consultation and I can gather your details to get started.

qaPairs.question: What types of cancer does Moffitt treat?
qaPairs.answer: Moffitt treats dozens of cancer types, from breast, lung, and colorectal cancers to leukemias, glioblastoma, and rare tumors. Tell me the diagnosis or concern and I will schedule you with the right specialty team.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer CAR T-cell therapy and immunotherapy?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, Moffitt is a leader in immunotherapy including CAR T-cell and cellular therapies. I can set up a consultation with the appropriate treatment team to review your options.

qaPairs.question: Can I get a bone marrow transplant at Moffitt?
qaPairs.answer: Moffitt has a dedicated Blood and Bone Marrow Transplant program offering autologous and allogeneic transplants. Let's book an evaluation so a specialist can review your case.

qaPairs.question: How much does treatment cost?
qaPairs.answer: Costs vary by treatment plan and insurance, so our financial counseling team provides personalized cost estimates and insurance verification. Let's get your consultation booked and I will connect you with those resources.

qaPairs.question: Do you accept my insurance?
qaPairs.answer: Moffitt works with many insurance plans as well as Medicare, and our Patient Access team verifies your specific coverage. Share your carrier and I will note it while we schedule your visit.

qaPairs.question: Where is Moffitt located?
qaPairs.answer: Moffitt has cancer hospitals and outpatient centers across the Tampa Bay area of Florida. Tell me your ZIP code and I will confirm the most convenient location for your appointment.

qaPairs.question: How do I enroll in a clinical trial?
qaPairs.answer: We offer many clinical trials including Phase 1 studies, and eligibility is determined during your evaluation. Let's schedule a consultation so a specialist can review whether a trial fits your situation.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer genetic testing for cancer risk?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our genetic counseling and testing team provides hereditary cancer risk assessment and lab panels. I can book you a genetic counseling appointment to get started.

qaPairs.question: Can I get a cancer screening like a mammogram or lung CT?
qaPairs.answer: Moffitt offers early-detection screenings including mammography, colonoscopy, and low-dose CT lung screening. Let's schedule the screening appointment that fits your needs.

qaPairs.question: How soon can I be seen?
qaPairs.answer: We work to see new patients as quickly as possible, especially for urgent concerns. Tell me how soon you would like to be seen and I will find the earliest available appointment.

qaPairs.question: What should I bring to my first appointment?
qaPairs.answer: Please bring your insurance card, photo ID, and any prior records, imaging, or pathology if available. I can send a full checklist once we confirm your appointment.

qaPairs.question: Do you treat patients from out of state or other countries?
qaPairs.answer: Moffitt serves patients from across the U.S. and internationally. Let's book your consultation and our team can help coordinate travel and records ahead of time.

qaPairs.question: What is precision medicine at Moffitt?
qaPairs.answer: Precision medicine uses molecular and genomic tumor profiling to personalize your treatment plan. I can schedule a consultation where a specialist explains how it applies to your case.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer fertility preservation before treatment?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, Moffitt offers fertility preservation such as egg, sperm, and embryo preservation before treatment begins. Let's book a consultation quickly since timing matters.

qaPairs.question: Can I speak with someone about palliative or supportive care?
qaPairs.answer: Our supportive and palliative care team helps with symptom management, pain control, and rehabilitation. I can schedule you a supportive care appointment alongside your treatment.

qaPairs.question: How do I refill my specialty pharmacy medication?
qaPairs.answer: Our specialty pharmacy handles oral oncolytics and complex medications with dedicated medication management. I can connect you with the pharmacy team or set up a follow-up appointment.

qaPairs.question: Can appointments be virtual?
qaPairs.answer: Moffitt offers virtual consultations for many visit types depending on your needs. Let me know your preference and I will schedule an in-person or virtual appointment.

qaPairs.question: How do I get started as a new patient right now?
qaPairs.answer: I can begin your new patient scheduling right here by asking a few quick questions. Let's start with your cancer type or reason for the visit.
